title: Total Bernoulli weight of restrictions leaving a coordinate free
statement:
Fix a real parameter $p$ and a coordinate $i$ among the $n$ variables. Summing the Bernoulli weight of $\rho$ over all restrictions $\rho$ on $n$ variables that leave $i$ free — that is, those for which $i$ is a free variable of $\rho$ — gives
\[
  \sum_{\rho \,:\, i \text{ free in } \rho} p^{\,|F(\rho)|}\left(\tfrac{1-p}{2}\right)^{\,n-|F(\rho)|} = p,
\]
where $F(\rho)$ denotes the set of free variables of $\rho$.
hypotheses_covered: coordinate i among the n variables
sum ranges over all restrictions on n variables
each term is the Bernoulli weight of the restriction
indicator selects restrictions leaving coordinate i free
replaced:
For each coordinate $i$, the Bernoulli($p$)-weighted sum over all restrictions of the indicator
that $i$ is free equals $p$; that is, $\E[\mathbf{1}[i \in J]] = p$.
